claims: "separate from the 6% national minimum wage increase" (also line 38: "rose 6% to $26.44 an hour")
whys: $24.95 to $26.44 is +5.97%, which is the figure the brief lists as correct. 6% is a rounded, hard-coded figure, not a value derived from code. lib/news.ts line 70 also says 6%.
constants: lib/constants/australian-tax.ts EMPLOYMENT.minimumWageHourly / minimumWageHourlyPrevious (derive the % from these)
reviewerNotes: I endorse the writer's fact questions: the rounded 6% vs 5.97% NMW; 'uniformly across every modern award' vs the C13/C14 5.95% rise; junior rates moving by the 'same 4.75%'; 'after' vs 'on or after 1 July'; C13 5.95% vs 5.97%; and the C13 article claiming 3 stages while also saying 'could complete it over two more reviews or spread it further'. These were left for a human to decide, not changed in this pass.

claims: "The 4.75% increase applies uniformly across every modern award" (also lead line 8: "Every modern award minimum rate rises 4.75%")
whys: The sibling C13 article says C13 and C14 rose 5.95% (4.75% plus an extra 1.2%) in the same review. So not every award minimum rate rose a uniform 4.75%.

claims: "apply the new rates from the first full pay period after 1 July 2026"
whys: The decision says "on or after 1 July 2026" (minimum-wage.ts NMW_DECISION.operativeNote), and so do the lead and the key facts on this page. lib/news.ts line 119 (description) also says "after".

claims: "Junior, apprentice and trainee rates ... move by the same 4.75%"
whys: Under the Manufacturing Award, junior percentages attach to the C13 / V2 rate (modern-awards.ts lines 753-754 and 867-869), and C13 rose more than 4.75%. The 18 to 20 junior transition from 1 Dec 2026 (minimum-wage.ts header) also changes junior rates separately.
constants: lib/constants/modern-awards.ts junior base level; lib/constants/junior-rates.ts JUNIOR_TRANSITION_SCHEDULES

claims: "C13 rates rise by 5.95% in total" (also lead line 10, key facts line 16, and lib/news.ts line 160 FAQ)
whys: modern-awards.ts line 779 gives C13 / V2 as $26.44, which equals the NMW. The NMW and C13 were both $24.95 before, and $24.95 to $26.44 is +5.97%, not 5.95%. Check whether the extra amount is 1.2% or about 1.22%.
constants: lib/constants/modern-awards.ts C13 / V2 row (line 779); lib/constants/australian-tax.ts EMPLOYMENT.minimumWageHourlyPrevious

claims: "junior, apprentice and trainee loadings continue to be calculated off the adjusted base rate at each stage"
whys: Apprentice rates in many awards are a percentage of the tradesperson (C10) rate, not the C13 base. Check whether the claim holds for apprentices.

claims: FTB Part A $306.46 "for each child aged 13 to 15", "up a few dollars on last year's rates"
whys: The constant is age13to19 (centrelink-family-payments.ts:197), so the 13 to 15 band is narrower than the rate's real coverage (16 to 19 in secondary study gets it too). 'A few dollars' has no 2025-26 figure to back it.
